text:
Lina Chen: Quick copy + a11y review: our 'Revoke API key' modal feels abrupt and a little scary. Screenshot: https://redwood/mockups/revoke-dialog.png

Alex Patel: Totally. Also saw that keyboard focus currently lands on the red action button \\u2014 we should avoid that. :grimacing:

Maya Singh: Yep. Default focus on the safe action (Cancel). And we should be explicit about impact in one line so non-technical admins aren't surprised.

Chris O'Neil: Draft proposal:

```
Headline: "Revoke API key?"
Body: "This key will stop working immediately. Update clients before revoking."
Buttons: [Cancel] [Revoke key]
```

Notes: Make Cancel the default focus. Enter should not trigger Revoke by default. Add aria-describedby linking to the body copy so screen readers announce the impact.

Lina Chen: I tried a slightly more explicit body: "This key will stop working immediately and any in-flight requests may fail. Create a replacement key before revoking." Might be too wordy for a modal.

Alex Patel: I prefer the shorter line and a link to docs for details. Keep modal concise.

Maya Singh: Accessibility checklist to include in the PR:
- Focus trap while dialog open
- Default focus on Cancel (safe action)
- Esc closes dialog and cancels
- Pressing Enter when Cancel is focused should activate Cancel, not Revoke
- Visible focus ring on both buttons
- Destructive button gets `aria-label="Revoke API key: <key-name>"` for clarity

DesignBot: Created a11y ticket: "dialog/revoke-key - default focus and semantics". See /docs/a11y/dialogs#revoke-key for pattern.

Chris O'Neil: One more UX nit: add a micro-tooltip on the API keys list row: "Revoking is irreversible — create replacement first." Keep it short.

Lina Chen: I'll update Figma and open a small PR with the new copy, tooltip text, and a11y changes. Will link to the API keys doc.

Alex Patel: @Maya can you review once PR is up?

Maya Singh: Happy to.

Lina Chen: Thanks all :thumbsup:
